explanation: The chapter in the Hebrew Bible and Old Testament that describes the wanderings of the children of Israel in the wilderness.
An expression referring to the descendants of the patriarch Jacob, also called Israel, which includes the twelve tribes of Israel.
The period of 40 years when the Israelites wandered through the wilderness after fleeing Egypt, before arriving in Canaan, the promised land.
The prophet and leader of the children of Israel, who received the Ten Commandments and led them out of slavery in Egypt and through the wilderness.
Describes the various places where the children of Israel camped during their wilderness journey. Genesis 33 lists a total of 42 stages.
The promised land that God pledged to give to Abraham's descendants. Today's Israel, Palestine, and parts of Lebanon and Jordan make up historical Canaan.
Moses' brother and the first high priest of Israel. He played an important role both in the exodus from Egypt and during the time in the wilderness.
